analysis.is_complaint_reason: The customer expresses dissatisfaction that their debit card was blocked abroad and says this cost them £47 in roaming charges, which is a financial loss under CH-1.
analysis.summary: [PERSON_1]'s debit card was blocked by the bank's fraud system on 18/10 while they were on holiday in Spain. They could not pay their hotel. They spent about two hours on the phone to get the card unblocked (call records show 1h52m). The block was lifted after ID&V. The customer says the call cost £47 in roaming charges and wants the £47 back. No fraud is alleged: this is a complaint about a precautionary fraud block. Loss is under £100, so severity is Low. It can be handled by the complaints handler.

timeline.event: Fraud block placed on the debit card while the customer was in Spain; lifted after ID&V following a call of 1h52m
Complaint received by email asking for £47 roaming charges back
Handler noted the block details, the call duration, no vulnerability and an email contact preference

analysis.severity_reason: The claimed financial loss is £47, which is under £100. No fraud is alleged, no vulnerability is noted, and there is no legal or media threat.

vulnerability.suggested_support: None identified. Note that 'No vulnerability' is recorded, but the case does not say the customer was asked about support needs. The handler may wish to confirm this sensitively.

analysis.routing_reason: This is a correctly operating precautionary fraud block, with no disputed or unauthorised payment, no scam, no lending issue and no systemic indicator. It does not meet any ESC-1 trigger, so the complaints handler should resolve it.
